FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Cement and 
Concrete Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 


In India, Portland cement clinker has been regularly supplied to various independent units ranging from large 
grinding stations to mini cement plants to produce all common varieties of cement used in construction. In view 
of global competitiveness of Indian cement manufacturing, clinker is also exported to different countries. 


At present, the concerned Indian Standard specifications for cement, for quality requirements of clinker, refer to 
the chemical requirements prescribed for cement in the Indian Standard specifications for ordinary Portland 
cement. In view of the increased use of clinker as tradable commodity and in order to provide a common standard 
reference for this material, these specifications are laid down to cover requirements of clinker as a separate 
standard. 


The composition of the technical committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


This standard lays down minimum requirements expected from clinker to the used for manufacture of various 
types and grades of cements. However, depending upon the special intended requirements of a particular type or 
grade of cement, the manufacturer may design for appropriate additional requirements of clinker, if so desired 
subject to compliance of the minimum requirements specified in this standard. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is compiled with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that specified value in this standard. 


IS 16353 : 2015 


Indian Standard 
PORTLAND CEMENT CLINKER — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers various requirements such as, 
manufacture, chemical and physical requirements, 
storage and transportation of Portland cement clinker 
used to produce cement meeting relevant Indian 
Standard specifications. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provision which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreement based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title

reinforced concrete (fourth revision).

4845 : 1968 Definitions and terminology relating 
to hydraulic cement 

3 TERMINILOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 4845 shall apply. 


4 MANUFACTURE 


Portland cement clinker consisting mainly of calcium 
silicates, aluminates and ferrites shall be obtained by 
heating to incipient fusion, a pre-determined and 
homogenous mixture of materials principally 


consisting of lime (CaO), and silica (SiO,) with smaller 
proportions of alumina (A1,O,) and iron oxide (Fe,O;). 


5 CHEMICAL REQUIREMENTS 


The Portland cement clinker shall conform to the 
chemical requirements given in Table 1, when tested 
in accordance with the methods given in IS 4032. For 
the purpose, the representative clinker shall be ground 
to pass 150 um IS sieve and tested. 


6 PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 


6.1 For checking its conformity, the cement produced 
out of the clinker shall conform to the requirements 
given in Table 2. For the purpose, the clinker shall be 
ground to a fineness of 220 + 25 m?/kg [when tested 
as per IS 4031 (Part 2)] with appropriate quantity of 
gypsum to obtain cement having not more than 3.5 
percent SO3. 


6.2 In order to regulate the quality of clinker supplied in 
terms of its particle size, the purchaser and the supplier 
may mutually decide the accepted particle size 
distribution of clinker. As a general guidance, the particle 
size distribution given in Table 3 may be followed. 


7 TRANSPORTATION OF CLINKER 


7.1 Portland cement clinker shall be supplied duly 
covered in trucks or suitable railway wagons or in ships 
or barges of suitable capacity. The supplier and the 
purchaser shall ensure that clinker is transported in 
environmental friendly manner minimizing dust 
pollution and spillage of clinker. 


7.2 For exports, clinker shall be supplied in suitable 
vessels with covered top to avoid any contact with 
moisture or sea water, supplier shall ensure that clinker 
is transported to water front or loading terminals in 
environmentally friendly manner. 


8 STORAGE 


Portland cement clinker shall be stored in such a 
manner as to permit easy access for proper inspection 
and to protect it from deterioration during storage. It 
shall be stored in proper storage area to protect it from 
entry of moisture or any other contamination; and can 
be stored in covered gantry or silo. If stored in an open 
area, it shall be ensured to place it on PCC floor and 
covered with tarpaulin to avoid loss of quality.

A Alkali-aggregate reactions have been noticed in aggregates in some parts of the country. On large and important jobs where concrete is 
likely to be exposed to humid atmosphere or wetting action, it is advisable that the aggregate be tested for alkali-aggregate reaction. In 
the case of reactive aggregates, the use of cement with alkali content below 0.6 percent expressed as sodium oxide (Na2O) that is, 
equivalent alkalies (NayO+0.658 KOL is recommended. Where, however, such cements are not available, use of alternative means 
may be resorted to for which a reference may be made to 8.2.5.4 of IS 456. If so desired by the purchaser, the manufacturer shall carry 
out test on Portland cement clinker for alkali content and report the result.

9 MANUFACTUER’S CERTIFICATE 


The manufacturer shall furnish a certificate to the 
purchaser or his representative within ten days of 
despatch of the Portland cement clinker stating that 
the material conforms to all the requirements of this 
standard, giving all test results except for compressive 
strength at 672 h + 4 h, which shall be furnished 
immediately after completion of the test. 


10 DELIVERY AND MARKING 


10.1 Supplies of Portland cement clinker in bulk shall 
be made by agreement between the purchaser and the 
supplier. Each consignment shall be accompanied by 
a certificate bearing the manufacturer’s name or his 
registered trade-mark, if any, the quantity of clinker 
and the words ‘Portland cement clinker’. 


10.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The consignments of Portland cement clinker may also 
be marked with the Standard Mark. 


10.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules 
and Regulations made thereunder. The details of 
conditions under which a licence for the use of the 


Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian 
Standards. 


11 SAMPLING 


11.1 A sample or samples for testing may be taken by 
the purchaser or his representative, or by any person 
appointed to superintend the work for purposes of 
which the Portland cement clinker is required or by 
the latter’s representative. 


11.1.1 The samples shall be taken within three weeks 
of the delivery and all the tests shall be commenced 
within one week of sampling. 


11.1.2 When it is not possible to test the samples within 
one week, the samples shall be packed and stored in 
airtight containers and tested at the earliest but not later 
than 3 months since the receipt of samples for testing. 


11.2 The scale of sampling and criteria for conformity 
shall be as prescribed in Annex A. 


11.3 The manufacturer or supplier shall afford every 
facility, and shall provide all labour and materials for 
taking and packing the samples for testing the Portland 
cement clinker and for subsequent identification of the 
Portland cement clinker samples. 


12 TESTS 


12.1 The sample or samples of Portland cement clinker 


IS 16353 : 2015 


for test shall be taken as described in 11 and shall be 
tested in the manner described in the relevant clauses 
of this standard. 


12.2 Independent Testing 


12.2.1 If the purchaser or his representative requires 
independent tests, the samples shall be taken before or 
immediately after delivery at the option of the 
purchaser or his representative, and the tests shall be 
carried out in accordance with this standard on the 
written instructions of the purchaser or his 
representative. 


12.2.2 After a representative sample has been drawn, 
tests on the sample shall be carried out as expeditiously 
as possible. 


13 REJECTION 


Portland cement clinker shall be rejected, if it does not 
comply with any of the requirements of this 
specification or purchaser specification, whichever is 
higher. Rejected clinker shall be separately stored with 
proper identification. Portland cement clinker 
remaining in bulk storage at the plant, prior to 
shipment, for more than six months, or in local storage 
in the hands of a vendor for more than three months 
after completion of the tests, may be retested for 
physical requirements before use and may be rejected, 
if it fails to conform to any of the requirement of this 
standard. 


ANNEX A 
(Clause 11.2) 
SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR CLINKERS 


A-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 


A-1.1 Lot 


The quantity of clinker from the same manufacturing 
unit and offered for inspection at one time not 
exceeding 2 000 t shall constitute a lot. 


The samples shall be selected and examined for each 
lot separately for ascertaining their conformity to the 
requirements of this standard. 


A-2 SAMPLING FROM BULK STORAGE (SILOS) 


A-2.1 Sub-lots 


For the purpose of sampling, the quantity of clinker in 


the bulk storage shall be divided into number of sub- 
lots depending upon the mass of the lot, in accordance 
with Table 4. 


Table 4 Number of Sub-lots into which a Lot is to 
be Divided 
(Clauses A-2.1, A-3.2 and A-4.2) 


Sl Mass of the Lot Number of Sub-Lots 
No. t 

(1) (2) (3) 

i) Up to 100 2 

ii) 101 to 200 3 

iii) 201 to 300 4 

iv) 301 to 500 5 

v) 501 to 1 000 6 

vi) 1 001 to 2 000 7 


IS 16353 : 2015 


A-2.2 Gross Sample 


The gross sample shall be taken from a sub-lot by 
taking increments at regular intervals when the Portland 
cement clinker is being charged into the bulk storage 
or is being discharged from the bulk storage. If there 
is more than one opening for charging or discharging, 
the increments shall be taken from each opening. 
Increments shall be taken from each sub-lot and each 
increment shall weigh at least 2 kg. It shall be ensured 
that the quantity of sample so collected is sufficient 
for tests prescribed in this standard. 


A-3 SAMPLING FROM WAGONS OR TRUCKS 


A-3.1 This method shall apply when Portland cement 
clinker in bulk is received in wagons or trucks. 


A-3.2 Sub-lots 


For the purpose of sampling, the quantity of Portland 
cement clinker in wagons or trucks shall be divided 
into a number of sub-lots depending upon the mass of 
the lot, in accordance with Table 4. The sub-lots shall 
consist of approximately equal number of wagons or 
trucks. Minimum two trucks/wagons shall be selected 
at random from each sub-lot. 


A-3.3 Gross Sample 


The gross sample shall be taken from a sub-lot with 
the help of a suitable sampler by taking increments of 
not less than 2 kg from 6 evenly distributed points in 
each selected wagon or truck and the mass of gross 
sample shall be minimum 24 kg. 


A-4 SAMPLING FROM SHIPS AND BARGES 


A-4.1 This method shall apply when clinker in bulk is 
received in ships or barges. 


A-4.2 Sub-lots 


For the purpose of sampling, the quantity of clinker in 


a ship or barge shall be divided into a number of sub- 
lots depending upon the mass of lot, in accordance with 
Table 4. 


A-4.3 Gross Sample 


The gross sample shall be taken from a sub-lot with 
the help of suitable sampler by taking increments at 
regular intervals when Portland cement clinker is being 
loaded into or discharged from the ship or the barge. 
Increments shall be taken from each sub-lot and each 
increment shall weigh at least 2 kg, and the mass of 
gross sample shall be minimum 24 kg. 


A-5 REDUCTION OF GROSS SAMPLE 


A-5.1 Equal quantities of the material shall be taken 
from each of the gross sample representing the sub-lot 
into which the lot has been divided and mixed together 
to constitute a composite sample representing the lot 
as a whole. The mass of the composite sample shall be 
about 24 kg. 


A-5.2 The composite sample shall be divided into 3 
equal parts; one for the purchaser, another for the 
supplier and the third to be used as a referee sample, 
The referee sample shall be used in case of a dispute 
between the purchaser and the supplier. Each of these 
parts shall then be placed in a suitable container and 
labelled with full identification particulars, such as 
supplier’s name, lot number, sub-lot number, date of 
sampling, etc. 


A-6 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


A-6.1 A composite sample shall be tested for all the 
requirements specified in this standard. 


A-6.2 All the test results shall satisfy the requirements 
of the standard to declare the conformity of the lot. 


IS 16353 : 2015

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 02 (7922).
